tips.title: Choosing the right plastic sheet
tips.text: When selecting plastic sheets for a scale model, consider the type of plastic and its thickness. For example, 0.5mm thick HIPS (High Impact Polystyrene) sheets from Plastruct are ideal for building model structures, while 1.5mm thick ABS sheets from Evergreen are better suited for creating model wheels and other details.

tips.title: Selecting the right adhesive
tips.text: For bonding plastic sheets, use a cyanoacrylate adhesive such as Tamiya's Extra Thin Cement, which dries quickly and forms a strong bond. Avoid using adhesives that can melt or warp the plastic, such as hot glue.

tips.title: Priming plastic sheets
tips.text: Before painting, prime plastic sheets with a coat of primer to ensure better paint adhesion and a smooth finish. Use a primer specifically designed for plastics, such as Tamiya's Plastic Primer, which is available in a range of colors.

tips.title: Sourcing scale model materials
tips.text: Shop online at retailers like HobbyTown, Michael's, or Hobby Lobby for a wide selection of scale model materials and supplies. Look for sales and discounts to stock up on materials at a lower cost.

tips.title: Storing scale model materials
tips.text: Store plastic sheets and other materials in a dry, dust-free area, away from direct sunlight. Use airtight containers or plastic bins with lids to keep materials fresh and protected from damage.
